About Mumei Shudan

Our history, philosophy, and commitment to authentic Aikido training

Our Story

Mumei Shudan Singapore was founded in 2009 by expert instructors trained in Japan, France and the US. The Dojo provides training in Aikido and follows the practice guidance from the Aikikai foundation; where its founders originate from. The dojo was initiated with 8 members and has reached more than 300 members and growing with new members and affiliation of new dojos. All Mumei Shudan instructors are certified by the Aikikai Foundation Aikido World Headquarters in Tokyo.

What is Aikido?

Aikido (合気道) is a modern Japanese martial art developed by Morihei Ueshiba (1883-1969), often referred to as O-Sensei (Great Teacher). Unlike many martial arts that focus on defeating opponents, Aikido emphasizes harmony, redirecting energy, and protecting both yourself and your attacker from harm.

The word "Aikido" can be broken down into three characters:

  • AI (合) - Harmony, joining, or blending
  • KI (気) - Spirit, energy, or life force
  • DO (道) - Way or path

Together, Aikido means "The Way of Harmony with Energy" or "The Way of Unifying Life Energy."

Core Principles of Our Practice

Non-Resistance

We blend with an attacker's energy rather than opposing it directly. This principle applies both on and off the mat.

Mutual Respect

Training partners work together for mutual benefit. There are no winners or losers, only fellow travelers on the path.

Natural Movement

Techniques are based on natural body mechanics and circular motion, making them efficient and sustainable.

Center & Balance

All movement originates from our center (hara). Maintaining balance - physical and mental - is fundamental.

Mind-Body Unity

Aikido training cultivates the integration of mind, body, and spirit through mindful practice.

Protection

The goal is to neutralize aggression while minimizing harm to all parties involved.

Our Training Philosophy

At Mumei Shudan, we believe that Aikido is more than just a martial art - it's a path of personal development that extends far beyond the dojo mat. Our training philosophy encompasses:

Progressive Learning

We structure our curriculum to build skills progressively, ensuring students develop a solid foundation before advancing to more complex techniques.

Individual Growth

Each student's journey is unique. We celebrate personal progress rather than competition, fostering an environment where everyone can thrive at their own pace.

Traditional Values, Modern Application

While we honor the traditional teachings and etiquette of Aikido, we also help students apply these principles to contemporary life challenges.

Safe Training Environment

Safety is paramount. We emphasize proper ukemi (falling/rolling safely) and appropriate technique application to minimize injury while maximizing learning.

Our Community

Mumei Shudan is more than a training facility - it's a community. Our students range from teenagers to retirees, from complete beginners to experienced martial artists. What unites us is a shared commitment to personal growth, mutual respect, and the pursuit of Aikido's principles.

We regularly host:

  • Weekend seminars with visiting instructors
  • Social events and dojo gatherings
  • Testing opportunities for rank advancement
  • Community outreach and demonstrations
